name: Divide Depot, Colorado Midland Railroad: 'All change for Cripple Creek'
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Men in winter clothes in front of the depot; a Colorado Midland train on the track in front of it; snow patches. Copied from 'Cripple Creek and Colorado Springs Illustrated' (1896), p. 101; the library's copy negative also carries printed text from that book. This is the depot before the 1903 rebuild that secondary sources report, so it is not the standing building. Looked at before use: the library's display copy is the photograph alone (the book text on the copy negative is not in it). A 'DIVIDE' board hangs from the depot, so the place is certain.
holder: Denver Public Library, Western History Collection

name: Pike's Peak from the Divide
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Stereograph: snow-covered Pikes Peak with a gabled wood-frame building, trees and fence. The library files it under Divide (Teller County); the date range is before the railway, and that it is this Divide has not been checked. A stereograph card ('Colorado Scenery', 'Pike's Peak from the Divide') shown whole. That it is this Divide rests on the library's subject heading.

name: Engineers Camp on Divide, CMRR (Colorado Midland Railway)
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Men holding surveying equipment in front of several log buildings; the library places it at Divide. PPLD's own rights line is 'In Copyright - Educational Use' and asks for reuse to be requested; the owner's report of permission covers PPLD. Not shown: the picture shows log cabins in dense forest under high snow peaks, which does not look like the open park country at Divide (Teller County); 'Divide' here is more likely the Continental Divide on the Colorado Midland's line further west. Kept as a record, not shown on this page, until its place is settled.
